title: Audio-Technica ATH-R50X Open-Back Headphones $268.91 (RRP $399) Delivered @ Amazon US via AU
body:
Deal: Audio-Technica ATH-R50X Open-Back Headphones $268.91 (RRP $399) Delivered @ Amazon US via AU

[The Magic Pudding] Have these guys learnt to make cables that don't disintegrate yet?
[camshandez] For real! I love my ATH-ADG1, had them in a cupboard for a couple years, picked them up and the cable has crumbled like a cookie 😳
[Faulty] I cut off the oem cable and replaced it with a female 3.5mm jack in the earcup body. Can use whatever cable I want now, a worthwhile mod.
[japes] I did this as well, so good as I love my ADG1X's.
[Skinnerr] How to replace a cable like that? Soldering?
[japes] They've finally realised detachable cables are necessary.
[Mugsy] Are these good for use with a top of the line electronic drum kit? Looking for a present for wife.
[GunnerMcDagget] Yes and no. They are good, but for an electronic drum kit you're better off with the ATH-M50/M50x as it's closed back so you're less likely to hear the constant drum taps and less likely to hear any other noise pollution (for example, your kids or someone watching TV in another room)
[jasswolf] For open back, I'd suggest the Aune AR3000 (launching soon) via AliE sales/stacks, the Aune AR5000 MK2 via AliE (~$300 AUD with sales/stacks), and the Sennheiser HD 600 or 650 ($250ish in local sales), but keep in mind you're wrestling with a bass roll-off after about 60Hz, though not so with the Aune although they are on the heavier side so may not be ideal for your wife.
For closed back if she needs the isolation and further bass extension, there's the Sennhesier HD 480 Pro for under $500 (expected sale price upcoming), but back more towards this price range it would be a Sennheiser HD 620 if she can EQ it for sub $250 on sale, or the FiiO FT1 for sub-$200 via AliExpress (maybe even sub-$150). FiiO and HD 620 are notably more heavy than the 480 Pro.
[jasswolf] https://www.ozbargain.com.au/comment/17999267/redir
[GunnerMcDagget] I personally don't like these ones. The ATH-m50x are some of the best closed back monitors, but it doesn't really translate that well to open back. Still sounds great, but the DT 990 Pro are better and usually cheaper. And yes, the 250 Ohm version is the one you find cheaper which means you need something better to drive it, but you can often find the 80 Ohm version for a decent price.
(Disclaimer: Audio is a mix of Objective and Subjective and many will find the ATH better than the DT)
[BargainHunterD] Yep the ATH-M50x are awesome, i use them for djing and production.
